clue.text: Hear of cooks teaching scientific principle

indicators.note: asks the solver to listen to how the following words are pronounced, not how they are spelt

parts.note: cooks means boils, and teaching is lore, giving the spoken phrase BOILS LORE

explanation.surface: Someone is told about chefs giving lessons on a scientific rule.
explanation.walkthrough: BOILS LORE, said out loud, matches the name of Robert Boyle's gas law.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Boyle's law about gas pressure and volume is a basic rule of physics.

clue.text: Money made by old transport company on a ship

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the old national railway operator
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Profits earned by a former transport firm from a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal British slang for cash.

clue.text: Police force in Spar

parts.note: the Yard is short for Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police headquarters
an arm is a branch of the armed forces, hence a force

explanation.surface: Officers turn up at a Spar convenience store.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar looks like the shop chain; here it is a ship's spar.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a yard, the horizontal spar holding a square sail.

clue.text: Arizona lawman has to carry silencer?

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the famous marshal of Tombstone, Arizona
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A Wild West marshal must pack a gun silencer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug worn in the ear cuts out noise, so it acts as a silencer for the wearer.

clue.text: Threaten subordinate

definitions.meaning: to ... (or lour) is to look dark and menacing, as clouds do

explanation.surface: Bully someone beneath you.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a scowling sky or face; the other is lesser in status, as in the lower ranks.

clue.text: American lexicographer secures graduate for on-line position

indicators.note: the dictionary maker's name holds the degree letters fast inside it

parts.note: Noah Webster compiled the famous American dictionary
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A dictionary writer takes on a graduate for an internet job.
explanation.definitionFit: A webmaster is the person who runs a website, a job done on the internet.

clue.text: Return deposit, say, for dress

parts.note: to deposit something is to put it down
EG, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Bring back a payment made as security on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is an outfit, often an eye-catching one.

clue.text: Stomach what Le Pétomane did endlessly?

definitions.note: a noun used attributively, as in stomach ache, matching the adjective

indicators.note: the last letter of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: Le Pétomane was a French stage performer famed for controlled flatulence: a gas trick

explanation.surface: Can one stomach the act of a famously flatulent music-hall star?
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the belly, as in gastric flu.

clue.text: What King George VI presumably did for Sir Henry Cecil?

definitions.text: What King George VI presumably did for Sir Henry Cecil?

parts.words: What King George VI presumably did for Sir Henry Cecil?
parts.note: Henry Cecil was a famous racehorse handler; the clue plays on what a reigning monarch does and a horse-racing profession

explanation.surface: A king appears to have done a service for a famous figure of the racing world.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cecil was a celebrated British racehorse trainer; the surface hints at reigning, with King George VI also the name of a big race.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil's job was preparing racehorses, so the profession named is his.

clue.text: Prepare retrospective broadcast for 19:31?

parts.note: to prime is to make ready

indicators.note: looking back, so the word for broadcast runs backwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out a signal

explanation.surface: Get a repeat ready for the evening schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 and 31 are both prime numbers, so 19:31 is a time made of primes.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime time is the peak evening viewing slot, and 19:31 falls in it while being two primes.

clue.text: Song boasted about members of SAS?

parts.note: an air is a tune
crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Special forces soldiers sing a bragging anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: SAS looks like the British special forces; it is Scandinavian Airlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots and cabin staff of an airline such as SAS form its flying staff.

clue.text: Food, mostly simple, carried by coaster — quite the reverse

swaps the roles, so the drinks mat sits inside the shortened word
drop the last letter of the word for simple

parts.note: basic means simple
a coaster is a small mat for a drink

explanation.surface: Plain fare served on a drinks mat, or the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a fragrant long-grain rice, a staple food.

clue.text: Joiner mixes plaster

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A carpenter blends some plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A stapler fastens sheets of paper together, so it joins them.

clue.text: Settle on Scottish island with Georgia

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde
GE is the country code for Georgia

explanation.surface: Choose between a Scottish island and an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle matters is to sort them out or fix them.

clue.text: Go ahead bachelor guys meet irregularly

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are scattered out of order

explanation.surface: Permission given for a single man to meet some men now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases give polite permission, inviting someone to proceed.

clue.text: Gangster involved in illegal gambles for football and rugby?

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up inside the other
crooked, so the letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: Al Capone, the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster mixed up in unlawful bets on sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and rugby are both sports played with a ball, examples of the category.

clue.text: Elite exhibition's not finished for conductor

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite

indicators.note: the last letter of the show word is left off

parts.note: a rodeo is a show of cowboy skills

explanation.surface: A top-class show is still running for the orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests an orchestra; it is an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal that carries current, an electrical conductor.

clue.text: Publisher's toy dog

definitions.meaning: ... Books is a UK paperback imprint
... Toys was a British brand of die-cast model cars
the Welsh short-legged herding breed favoured by the Queen

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the imprint, the model-car brand, and the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a paperback imprint, a model-car maker and a Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Barchester chaplain cycles and runs

explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles' moves the S of SLOPE to the end.

clue.text: Bird in tree eating large insect's head

indicators.note: the tree swallows the other letters inside it

parts.note: the pecan is a hickory tree

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

clue.text: A wader's swimming downstream

indicators.note: the letters float about into a new order

clue.text: Parent organised river transport

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

clue.text: Laminate gold into lady's hat

clue.text: Slobbish house member involved in topless spree

the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a junket is a jaunt or spree

explanation.surface: A scruffy politician caught up in a raunchy night out.

clue.text: Hurt soldier is noble

parts.note: to gall is to vex or wound

clue.text: Food in South American state

HI is the postal code for Hawaii

explanation.surface: Eating out in a southern state of the USA.

clue.text: Look around King and Emperor's mountain retreat
